Markets will be closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving, and tech companies might just be thankful
for one less trading day.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq has been consistently trending down in November.
The S&P 500, Dow, and the Nasdaq are now all in correction territory, meaning they are

Stephen Bissaha, NPR News.
Diplomats meeting at the United Nations in Geneva have agreed to start discussing options
to regulate lethal, autonomous weapons often called killer robots.
The agreement falls far short of the legally binding rules demanded by many countries and
by the international Red Cross.
Emojin Folks reports from Geneva.
The technology exists to create weapons which can target and kill entirely on their own.
Dozens of countries want legally binding rules for such weapons.
But in Geneva, big powers, including the U.S. and Russia, were reluctant.
After days of talks dragged into the weekend, a watered-down agreement emerged.
Countries will spend two years discussing possible rules, which might be optional or
binding.
Diplomats say they were relieved to achieve something, but humanitarian organizations
and human rights groups say this was a missed opportunity to create rules which prevent
machines from deciding who to kill.
For NPR News, I'm Imogen Folks in Geneva.
This is NPR News in Washington.
U.N. climate talks broke down over the issue of fossil fuels and their impact on global
warming, Russia and Saudi Arabia led the way in excluding the issue.
Several countries and the 27-nation European Union opposed the final proposal as a result.
As smaller climate-vulnerable nations sought more decisive action, the U.S. did not participate
in those talks.
At least three workers are dead and dozens are missing after a fire tore through a candy
factory west of Indonesia's capital.
The company says about 300 workers were inside when the fire broke out yesterday.
Naina Rao has the latest from Jakarta.
The fire started Saturday evening at the three-story facility west of Jakarta.
The factory produces milk-based candies and snacks.
Indonesia's search and rescue agency is still searching for more than two dozen missing workers
after evacuating 15 people on Sunday.
Some are being treated at a local hospital for injuries.
Workers are using water cannons to cool remaining hot spots amidst the building debris as smoke
continues billowing from the remaining embers and the collapsed structure.
Officials say the fires have been put out.
A cause has not been confirmed.
For NPR News, I'm Naina Rao in Jakarta, Indonesia.
